flow.title: FakeCompany: The Carbon Platform Your Car Didn't Know It Needed

list.title: Step 1
beforeList: Setup takes so long that the intern who started it has since been promoted twice.
Plugging into the car's computer occasionally makes the radio play only polka.
afterList: Plug it in and it works faster than you can find the instruction manual.
No device? Just use your phone. Yes, the one you're already scrolling memes on.

list.title: Step 2
beforeList: Every car model speaks its own dialect, and half the data gets lost in translation.
afterList: Works with sedans, trucks, vans, and possibly that suspicious golf cart in the parking lot.
Already have devices installed? We'll befriend them via API. No awkward small talk.

list.title: Step 3
beforeList: Collecting paper fuel receipts by hand, including the ones that went through the washing machine.
Auditors ask for proof, and you hand them a shoebox full of crumpled paper.
afterList: Data collects itself and lives in the cloud, guarded more tightly than the office snack drawer.
Carbon numbers calculate themselves, so nobody has to blame the calculator anymore.

list.title: Step 4
beforeList: You get a pie chart. Then you stare at the pie chart. Then you get hungry for actual pie.
afterList: AI reads the charts so you can finally take that lunch break.
Up to 35% fewer emissions, and roughly 100% fewer headaches (unverified).
